newsitem.title: CANADA: Gardiner CEO says approached by many firms.
newsitem.headline: Gardiner CEO says approached by many firms.

text.p: Poco Petroleums Ltd was the most persistent of several companies interested in striking a deal to acquire Gardiner Oil & Gas Ltd, Gardiner chief executive Wayne Thomson said on Wednesday.

"We had been approached by a number of different companies and everybody was given the same answer, including Poco, that the company wasn't for sale," Thomson said in an interview. "Poco was more persistent.
The prospect of Gardiner shareholders becoming large shareholders in Poco tipped the scales in the suitor's favor, he said.
Poco said late Tuesday it would pay C$5 plus 0.6 of a Poco share for each Gardiner share in a friendly deal valued at C$225 million.
Gardiner shareholders representing 76 percent of the company's stock have signed lockup agrements not to tender to a competing bid unless it was over C$13.50 per share.
Shares of Gardiner, which owns western Alberta natural gas properties that are intertwined with Poco's, have climbed to C$11.50 from a year-low of C$5.88.
"If you take a straight cash position (in a buyout), your tax position is not great," Thomson said. "So, you really want a company that you've got some confidence in going into the future."
Scott Inglis, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital said he believed Poco was paying a fair price the Gardiner assets, that include a large undeveloped land spread.
Gardiner said its proved and probable reserves consist of 12 million barrels of oil and natural gas liquids and 200 billion cubic feet of gas, figures Inglis said were likely conservatively stated.
"I think (Poco will) prove that there's a lot of upside in the undeveloped land and there's a lot of reserves to be booked," he said.
Inglis said his projections for Poco as a result of the Gardiner deal included a C$0.10 increase in Poco's 1997 cash flow per share to C$2.15. Earnings per share were not expected to change, he said.
